title: Perfect annihilator for a map to a supported complex
statement: Let Y be quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-pc-scheme], let V be a quasi-compact open, and let T=Y\setminus V. For a morphism alpha:P\to Q in D_QCoh(Y) [def-pc-derived-category], assume either (i) P is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex] and Q is supported on T, or (ii) P is pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], Q is supported on T, and Q is bounded below. Then there is a morphism I\to\mathcal O_Y from a perfect complex I that is an isomorphism on V and for which I\otimes^L P\to Q, the composite of the tensor action with alpha, is zero.

proof.text: Put K=R\mathcal H om(P,Q). By [lem-sc-rhom-supported-qcoherent], in case (ii) K is quasi-coherent and bounded below, and in case (i) it is quasi-coherent; because Q is supported on T and internal Hom commutes with restriction to opens, K is supported on T. The morphism alpha corresponds by tensor-Hom adjunction to a morphism a:\mathcal O_Y[0]\to K.

The existing supported-generation statement [lem-sc-supported-derived-generated-perfect] supplies a perfect E supported on T and writes K as a sequential derived colimit 0=K_0\to K_1\to\cdots in D_QCoh(Y) whose successive cones are direct sums of shifts of E. The object \mathcal O_Y[0] is perfect, hence compact in D_QCoh(Y) by [lem-pc-perfect-object-compact]. Applying the compact-Hom hocolim statement [lem-pc-compact-hom-hocolim] in C=D_QCoh(Y) to K=\mathcal O_Y[0], the map a is represented by a map a_n:\mathcal O_Y[0]\to K_n at some finite stage n.

source.place: Tag 0E4G (Lemma 48.4.3), proof, together with Derived Categories Tag 094A

proof.text: If n=0 then a_n=0 and a factors through Q'=0. Otherwise apply [lem-sc-supported-factor-through-thick] in the ambient category C=D_QCoh(Y) (which has arbitrary direct sums) to the one-element family E, which is compact by [lem-pc-perfect-object-compact], and to the sequence X_m=K_m (m>=1): rotating the triangle K_m\to K_{m+1}\to C_m\to K_m[1] with C_m a direct sum of shifts of E gives C_m[-1]\to K_m\to K_{m+1}\to C_m, so Z_m=C_m[-1] is a direct sum of shifts of E, and X_1=K_1\cong C_0 is one as well. With the compact source \mathcal O_Y[0], the map a_n factors as \mathcal O_Y[0]\to Q'\to K_n with Q' in the thick subcategory generated by a finite direct sum of copies of E. Since E is perfect, Q' is perfect by [lem-pc-perfect-thick-closure] (triangulated subcategories of D_QCoh(Y) have their triangles distinguished in D(\mathcal O_Y)). The same operations preserve support on T: shifts and sums preserve vanishing after restriction to V, cones do so by the long exact cohomology sequence, and direct summands do so by restriction. Hence Q' is perfect and supported on T, and a factors through Q'.

source.place: Tag 09SP (Lemma lemma-factor-through), with the supported-generator properties from Tag 0E4G

proof.text: Complete \mathcal O_Y[0]\to Q' to a distinguished triangle I\to\mathcal O_Y[0]\to Q'\to I[1]. Restriction to V is triangulated, and Q'|_V=0 because Q' is supported on T=Y\setminus V, so I\to\mathcal O_Y[0] restricts to an isomorphism on V. Since \mathcal O_Y[0] and Q' are perfect, I is perfect by [lem-pc-perfect-thick-closure] (1). The composite I\to\mathcal O_Y[0]\to Q'\to K is zero because a factors through Q'.

Under the tensor-Hom adjunction, the map I\to K is exactly the composite I\otimes^L P\to Q induced by alpha. Its vanishing therefore gives the required zero composite, while Step 4 gives the perfect complex and the isomorphism over V.
